images.caption: Figure 1:A recursion needs two channels: the outer loop sets the inner loop’s objective, and the inner loop, Proposer–Director self-play on a randomized rollout group, returns the evidence for withdrawing skills.

Figure 2:Paradigm comparison. (a) Learned orchestration trains on a hand-designedstatic curriculum. (b) Self-improving agents measure the frontier with skills present, askill-anchored frontierwhere advantages collapse once skills leave. (c) Skill scaffolds withdraw guidance throughsuccess-rate gates, unreliable evaluation signals pinned by self-play. (d) R2Orch nests two loops joined by downward (objective) and upward (evidence) channels.

Figure 3:Overview of R2Orch. Top: Proposer–Director self-play (inner loop) and skill withdrawal (outer loop) share one randomized rollout group. Bottom left: Recursive Learnability scores a task with the candidate skill hidden. Bottom right: Skill Withdrawal withdraws or admits each skill by the posterior of its paired contrast.
